newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast clips 96/97 coffee marketing rates.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast clips 96/97 coffee marketing rates.

text.p: Ivory Coast issued a full list of coffee marketing rates on Monday indicating a clip in rates for exporters and commissions they pass on to buyers, an official document shows.

A Caistab coffee and cocoa marketing agency document dated November 14 indicates a free-on-board rate of 650.895 CFA per kg of dehulled green coffee, including five CFA per kilo for the bag. The rates per kilo given are as follows:
- Farmgate price (bagged) 500 CFA for green unhulled graded coffee or 232.311 CFA for dehulled coffee beans;
- Transported to port, bagged, export prepared 621.867 CFA;
- With exporter commission/store-to-ship charges giving a pre-export tax (10 CFA per kg) guaranteed FOB rate of 640 CFA

The new rate per kilo of bagged dehulled coffee with exporters' commision, transport to port, and store-to-ship charges indicates a drop of 5 CFA from 1996/97 after deduction of rates for export prepared coffee.
In 1995/96 the two rates were 856.732 and 842.378 respectively but dehulled coffee bean prices were higher at 700 CFA per bagged kilo. Hulled beans were priced at 336.038 CFA per bag.
Ivory Coast set this year's price down in line with lower world market prices.
Buyers commissions in 1995/96 were also higher at 35.281 CFA.
Exporters were unavailable for comment on Monday night but said earlier that their GEPEX trade body was still locked in dispute with the Caistab over cocoa marketing rates issued last week.
The 1996/97 coffee prices and export taxes were announced on November 14 when Ivory Coast opened the new season but the full marketing list was until now unpublished.
The list was signed by the Caistab's new managing director Yves-Marie Koissy.
